Header: Bactrocera cucurbitae , B. dorsalis (previously B. invadens ), B. zonata Vidudu or Inzi ya matunda in Swahili

Prevention: Baby, which are not attractive to fruit flies because of hard skin.
Intercrop melons with repellent crops such as leek.
Avoid growing melons near mango trees because fruit flies will invade from there.
Avoid ripening of melons at the same time as mangoes.
Enhance build-up of natural enemies by avoiding use of agro- chemicals and mulching.
Apply mulch below melons to reduce fly egg laying (melon skins will not get softened by soil contact.)
Harvest melons nearing ripening; do not wait until total ripening of melons.
Remove non-harvested melons and wild pumpkins as they will host larvae.
Monitoring: Search twice a week for adult fruit flies on leaves and flowers during flowering and fruit on-set stage.
Look for adult flies on the flowers and fruits.
The adult fly is a winged insect, nearly 1cm long.
It is like a house fly but smaller, and with a nicely coloured body.
When 1-2 flies are detected per 20-40 plants, consider action.
For early detection, use commercial pheromone traps with trimedlure, cue lure, or methyl eugenol (3 traps/ km2).
Follow infestation regularly, once flies are detected.
Inspect fruits for soft black spotted ovi- punctures twice a week.
Larvae are yellowish whitish, 0.5-1 cm long and 2-3 mm thick.
When damage is detected on 1-2 melons /10m2 on average, consider acting quickly before more eggs are laid.
Direct Control: Collect all mature rotten melons from the field because they harbour fruit fly larvae.
Restrictions: Chemical sprays can rarely control adult fruit flies
because they migrate from neighbouring fields and rarely control the larvae because the adults lay their eggs inside the melons so larvae develop inside.
Wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Rimon10EC usually applied at 5-10 ml per 20 litres water, but check product label).
U (Unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use); pre- harvest interval 14 days, restricted re- entry interval 1day.
Apply at flowering stage early in the morning or late in the evening.
Attract and mass trap flies using 20-50 ml fermented brew or honey or 2 ml
GF120-bait with 10 ml trimedlure or methyl eugenol + little 1ml insecticide (e.g.
Nuvan) filled into pastic bottles with holes or into commercial traps.
Use 3 to 5 traps across a field per 1 acre.
This method only works if many farmers in the same area participate.
